title: [Đề 07] Bộ Đề Thực Chiến B1 Số 03 — Chuẩn Đầu Ra ULIS (Colouring Books for Adults)
description: Đề luyện thi thực chiến VNU Test Bậc 3 chuẩn hóa theo khung năng lực ngoại ngữ Bậc 3 (CEFR B1). Bài đọc thực tế: Colouring Books for Adults (Part 2), The 'I Love Italy' Photography Competition (Part 3), Karina Moore – Teenage High Diver! (Part 4).

tasks.title: Part 1: Signs & Notices
tasks.instructions: There are 7 questions in this part. Choose the best answer (A, B, or C) that matches the meaning of each sign, message, or notice.

questions.prompt:
John,
You know I said that football practice will be on Wednesday … Well, it isn’t – it’s on Thursday. Sorry! See you there.
Cheers,
Adam

Why has Adam written this message?

options.text: to ask if John wants to play football
to tell John that Adam can’t play football
to let John know about a change of plan

questions.explanationVi: Adam nhắn cho John rằng buổi tập bóng đá sẽ không diễn ra vào thứ Tư như đã nói trước đó mà đổi sang thứ Năm ('Well, it isn’t – it’s on Thursday'). Như vậy Adam viết tin nhắn để báo cho John biết về sự thay đổi kế hoạch ('a change of plan'). Đáp án C đúng.

questions.prompt:
SCHOOL FESTIVAL OF BOOKS
Meet Ralph Sparks.
Hear how he got ideas for his books, including History of Exploring the New World.
Thurs 9 a.m. Room D31.

Pupils can

options.text: come and listen to a writer.

questions.explanationVi: Thông báo Ngày hội Sách của trường mời học sinh đến gặp tác giả Ralph Sparks và lắng nghe ông chia sẻ cách lấy ý tưởng viết sách ('Meet Ralph Sparks. Hear how he got ideas for his books...'). Tức là học sinh có thể đến nghe một nhà văn trò chuyện. Đáp án C đúng.

questions.prompt:
Science Museum trip next Friday
Tickets are available for $4 (for coach transport to the museum, and for museum entry).
If you’re interested, see Mr Goss.

options.text: You can now buy tickets for the museum trip.
Tell Mr Goss how you want to travel to the museum.
Mr Goss will tell you if you need a ticket to the museum.

questions.explanationVi: Thông báo nêu: Vé cho chuyến tham quan Bảo tàng Khoa học thứ Sáu tuần sau hiện đã mở bán với giá $4 bao gồm cả xe đưa đón và vé vào cửa ('Tickets are available for $4... If you’re interested, see Mr Goss'). Tức là học sinh hiện đã có thể mua vé cho chuyến đi. Đáp án A đúng.

vocabularyNotes.meaning: vé vào cửa, sự đi vào

questions.prompt:
From: Lizzie
To: Jenny

Jenny,
I think I left my scarf in your flat after the party. Have you seen it? Otherwise I’ll buy another one.
Lizzie

Why has Lizzie written this?

options.text: to invite Jenny to a party
to tell Jenny about a shopping trip
to ask about something that she’s lost

questions.explanationVi: Lizzie nghĩ mình đã để quên chiếc khăn quàng cổ ở căn hộ của Jenny sau bữa tiệc nên viết thư hỏi xem Jenny có nhìn thấy nó không ('I think I left my scarf in your flat after the party. Have you seen it?'). Đáp án C đúng.

questions.prompt:
Hi Dave,
I broke my tennis racket. Can I use yours? I’ll give it back in maths tomorrow. By the way, wasn’t the homework difficult?
Mike

Mike wants to

options.text: get help from Dave with the homework.

questions.explanationVi: Mike làm gãy vợt tennis nên hỏi mượn vợt của Dave và hứa sẽ trả lại vào giờ Toán ngày mai ('I broke my tennis racket. Can I use yours? I’ll give it back in maths tomorrow'). Tức là Mike muốn mượn đồ của Dave. Đáp án B đúng.

questions.prompt:
Mr Gregson is away today.
Class 3, at 9 a.m., please go and join Class 4 in Room 7C for geography. Mr Gregson will be back tomorrow.

options.text: There isn’t a geography lesson tomorrow.
Class 4’s lesson is happening at a different time today.
There will be more people in Room 7C than usual today.

questions.explanationVi: Vì hôm nay thầy Gregson đi vắng, Lớp 3 sẽ sang học ghép môn Địa lý cùng với Lớp 4 tại Phòng 7C lúc 9 giờ sáng ('Class 3, at 9 a.m., please go and join Class 4 in Room 7C'). Vì hai lớp học chung một phòng nên Phòng 7C hôm nay sẽ đông học sinh hơn thường lệ. Đáp án C đúng.

questions.prompt:
DON'T LEAVE RUBBISH IN OUR WOODS
TAKE IT HOME!

options.text: Take away all rubbish, including that left by others.
Do not enter the woods at any time.
You cannot leave your rubbish here at all.

questions.explanationVi: Biển báo trong rừng nhắc nhở: Không để lại rác trong rừng của chúng tôi, hãy mang rác của bạn về nhà ('Don't leave rubbish in our woods – Take it home!'). Điều này có nghĩa là bạn hoàn toàn không được vứt lại rác ở đây. Đáp án C đúng.

tasks.title: Part 2: Cloze Test
tasks.instructions: Read the text below and choose the best answer (A, B, or C) for each blank from 8 to 15.

passage.title: Colouring Books for Adults
passage.text:
Many people probably used to spend time adding colour to pictures in colouring books when they were children. However, once people get older, very (8) ________ of them continue with the hobby. Instead, they (9) ________ their crayons away in the cupboard forever.

However, psychology researchers now think that even for adults, (10) ________ as little as ten minutes a day colouring pictures in this way can bring huge (11) ________. For example, some people say that it improves their (12) ________ for a while by making them feel more cheerful and generally calmer.

One reason for this may be that other activities (13) ________ with art, such as drawing or painting, can actually be quite stressful, especially if you don’t feel very successful (14) ________ it. But adding colour to a picture that’s already drawn for you (15) ________ only a low level of skill, so you can relax rather than becoming anxious about it!

questions.prompt: However, once people get older, very (8) ________ of them continue with the hobby.
questions.explanationVi: Đại từ 'them' thay thế cho 'people' (danh từ đếm được số nhiều), do đó dùng 'very few of them' (rất ít người trong số họ tiếp tục sở thích này). 'Little' và 'less' dùng cho danh từ không đếm được. Đáp án B đúng.

vocabularyNotes.meaning: rất ít (dùng cho danh từ đếm được)

questions.prompt: Instead, they (9) ________ their crayons away in the cupboard forever.
questions.explanationVi: Cụm động từ 'put something away' mang nghĩa 'cất cái gì đi (vào tủ)'. Khi lớn lên, người ta thường cất bút màu vào tủ mãi mãi. Đáp án C đúng.

questions.prompt: ...even for adults, (10) ________ as little as ten minutes a day colouring pictures in this way...
questions.explanationVi: Cấu trúc 'spend + time + V-ing' (dành ra chỉ 10 phút mỗi ngày để tô màu tranh: 'spending as little as ten minutes a day colouring pictures'). Đáp án B đúng.

questions.prompt: ...colouring pictures in this way can bring huge (11) ________.
questions.explanationVi: Cụm từ 'bring huge benefits' (mang lại những lợi ích to lớn). 'Interests' (sở thích/lợi tức) và 'favours' (ân huệ) không phù hợp ngữ cảnh. Đáp án A đúng.

questions.prompt: For example, some people say that it improves their (12) ________ for a while by making them feel more cheerful and generally calmer.
questions.explanationVi: Cụm 'improves their mood' (cải thiện tâm trạng của họ) vì vế sau giải thích nó giúp họ cảm thấy vui vẻ và bình tĩnh hơn ('making them feel more cheerful and generally calmer'). Đáp án B đúng.

questions.prompt: One reason for this may be that other activities (13) ________ with art, such as drawing or painting, can actually be quite stressful...
questions.explanationVi: Cấu trúc 'connected with something' (các hoạt động khác có liên quan đến nghệ thuật, chẳng hạn như vẽ tranh). Đáp án A đúng.

questions.prompt: ...especially if you don’t feel very successful (14) ________ it.
questions.explanationVi: Cấu trúc tính từ 'successful at (doing) something' (thành công, giỏi về việc thực hành một hoạt động nào đó). Đáp án B đúng.

vocabularyNotes.meaning: thành công, làm tốt việc gì

questions.prompt: But adding colour to a picture that’s already drawn for you (15) ________ only a low level of skill, so you can relax...
questions.explanationVi: Động từ 'requires' (đòi hỏi, yêu cầu): Việc tô màu vào bức tranh đã vẽ sẵn chỉ đòi hỏi mức kỹ năng thấp ('requires only a low level of skill'). 'Depends' phải đi với 'on'. Đáp án C đúng.

tasks.title: Part 3: True / False
tasks.instructions: Read the text below and decide whether statements from 16 to 20 are True or False. Choose A for True and B for False.

passage.title: The 'I Love Italy' Photography Competition
passage.text:
I LOVE ITALY
For your chance of winning a weekend in Bassano Del Grappa, Italy, tick the 'x' on your favourite photo from the images opposite! It only takes a bit of imagination to find yourself in Italy.

HOW TO ENTER:
Choose both your favourite photo and tell us what 'Imagine More' means to you and then return your completed leaflet to the address opposite or enter online.

WIN:
The winner will receive a weekend break for two people to include complimentary tickets to Bassano Fotografia 11, a diverse photographic exhibition hosted by Manfrotto School of Xcellence. A series of exhibitions, workshops and seminars on photography, delivered by internationally renowned photographers, will contribute in transforming Bassano Del Grappa into the centre of photography and imagination. Whether you are an amateur photographer or an expert, Bassano del Grappa has something to offer everyone: A weekend immersion in art, culture, landscapes and photography.

FULL DETAILS:
The prize includes return flights to Italy for two people, bed and breakfast accommodation for three nights in Bassano Del Grappa from a Thursday to Sunday in October 2011. Keen photographers will also have the opportunity to visit some incredible landscapes that lend themselves perfectly for photography courtesy of Manfrotto School of Xcellence.

TERMS AND CONDITIONS:
The 'I Love Italy' competition closes on 30th September 2011. All entries must be received by this date. Manfrotto Distribution Ltd accepts no responsibility for entries received after this date or for entries lost in transit. By entering this competition you will also be opting into Manfrotto Distribution Ltd and Manfrotto School of Xcellence (MSoX) e-newsletters, but you have the option to unsubscribe at any time. One entry per person only. Open to UK residents only. There is one prize (for two people) to Italy and it is not redeemable for cash.

questions.prompt: To enter the competition, you can also fill in the online form.
questions.explanationVi: Trong mục HOW TO ENTER nêu rõ: '...return your completed leaflet to the address opposite or enter online.' (Gửi tờ phiếu đã điền về địa chỉ đối diện hoặc đăng ký trực tuyến trên mạng). Nhận định là ĐÚNG (True - A).

questions.prompt: Bassano del Grappa has nothing to offer professional photographers.
questions.explanationVi: Trong mục WIN khẳng định: 'Whether you are an amateur photographer or an expert, Bassano del Grappa has something to offer everyone' (Dù bạn là người chụp ảnh nghiệp dư hay chuyên gia, Bassano del Grappa đều có những điều thú vị dành cho mọi người). Vì vậy nói nơi này không có gì cho nhiếp ảnh gia chuyên nghiệp là SAI (False - B).

questions.prompt: The prize includes a two-way journey by air.
questions.explanationVi: Trong mục FULL DETAILS ghi rõ: 'The prize includes return flights to Italy for two people...' ('return flights' là vé máy bay khứ hồi hai chiều, đồng nghĩa với 'a two-way journey by air'). Nhận định là ĐÚNG (True - A).

questions.prompt: All entries must be received no later than 30th September 2011.
questions.explanationVi: Trong mục TERMS AND CONDITIONS nêu rõ: 'The 'I Love Italy' competition closes on 30th September 2011. All entries must be received by this date.' ('by this date' đồng nghĩa với 'no later than 30th September 2011'). Nhận định là ĐÚNG (True - A).

vocabularyNotes.meaning: bài dự thi, phiếu đăng ký dự thi

questions.prompt: You cannot unsubscribe from e-newsletters.
questions.explanationVi: Trong mục TERMS AND CONDITIONS ghi rõ: '...e-newsletters, but you have the option to unsubscribe at any time.' (Bạn có quyền hủy đăng ký nhận bản tin điện tử bất cứ lúc nào). Do đó nhận định không thể hủy đăng ký là SAI (False - B).

tasks.title: Part 4: Reading Comprehension
tasks.instructions: Read the following passage and choose the best answer (A, B, or C) for each question from 21 to 25.

passage.title: Karina Moore – Teenage High Diver!
passage.text:
Several times a week, teenager Karina Moore trains at her local pool to jump from the high-diving board into the water – in an attempt to become a national diving champion.

Karina first learned about diving during a family break in Spain, where the resort’s pool had a high-diving board. Young people were diving off it, and it looked fun, but Karina didn’t join in, even though she was a strong swimmer. Then after returning home, she discovered a long-distance runner she’d always admired had started diving for relaxation – so she became more interested.

Karina joined a beginners’ diving class at her local pool. They had several sessions jumping onto soft materials before trying the high board. ‘The water looked a long way down,’ says Karina, ‘but after our training, I felt I’d handle it – without injuring myself! They’d warned me I’d land in the water fast – at around 60 kph – but I was prepared. I couldn’t wait to get started – although the others weren’t so keen! Anyway, I wasn’t disappointed by the experience.’

In Karina’s area, there’s now lots of interest in high diving, but it’s sometimes difficult for swimmers to find suitable practice facilities. Although the pools are deep enough, they’re in use so often by diving clubs that other people don’t get opportunities to practise. Fortunately, though, Karina’s coach noticed her talent and helped her develop her techniques. After only two years, she’s winning competitions in her area.

But what’s it like to concentrate so much on diving? ‘I train 20 hours a week,’ says Karina, ‘and I won’t pretend it’s easy – you have to enjoy it to spend so much time doing it! It’s not easy for my parents either, though – they drive me to training sessions early in the morning, and that costs money. But they’ve had financial help from sports organisations, luckily. And my schoolwork and social life are good. I still meet my mates – and there’s always the phone! The only thing I hadn’t realised was that the pool water would damage my hair – I used to love my long hair, but I’ve had to cut it short because it looked awful! But I’ll definitely keep on diving!’

questions.prompt: What made Karina keen to take up diving?

options.text: She wanted to repeat her holiday experience.
She found out her athletics hero had taken it up.
She’d visited a pool where some teenagers were doing it.

questions.explanationVi: Đoạn 2 nêu: Khi ở Tây Ban Nha cô không tham gia nhảy cầu, nhưng sau khi về nhà, cô phát hiện ra một vận động viên chạy đường dài mà cô luôn ngưỡng mộ đã bắt đầu tập nhảy cầu để thư giãn nên cô trở nên hứng thú ('she discovered a long-distance runner she’d always admired had started diving for relaxation – so she became more interested'). Đáp án B đúng.

vocabularyNotes.meaning: bắt đầu theo đuổi một môn thể thao/sở thích

questions.prompt: How did Karina feel the first time she used the high board?

options.text: worried about how far it was above the pool
pleased to experience it with other beginners
confident that she wouldn’t get hurt

questions.explanationVi: Đoạn 3 trích lời Karina: 'but after our training, I felt I’d handle it – without injuring myself!' (Sau quá trình tập luyện, cô tự tin mình sẽ xử lý tốt mà không làm bản thân bị thương). Đáp án C đúng.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about diving facilities in Karina’s area?

options.text: They’re not used as much as they could be.
There aren’t enough coaches teaching people to use them.
They’re not available to the public for long enough each day.

questions.explanationVi: Đoạn 4 viết: 'Although the pools are deep enough, they’re in use so often by diving clubs that other people don’t get opportunities to practise.' (Hồ bơi được các câu lạc bộ sử dụng thường xuyên đến mức người dân khác không có đủ thời gian/cơ hội để tập luyện). Đáp án C đúng.

vocabularyNotes.meaning: cơ sở vật chất, trang thiết bị

questions.prompt: How does Karina feel about spending so much time diving?

options.text: surprised by one effect it has had on her
sorry she no longer sees her friends so much
anxious about the amount of money it costs

questions.explanationVi: Ở đoạn cuối, Karina tâm sự: 'The only thing I hadn’t realised was that the pool water would damage my hair – I used to love my long hair, but I’ve had to cut it short because it looked awful!' (Điều duy nhất cô không ngờ tới là nước hồ bơi làm hỏng mái tóc dài khiến cô phải cắt ngắn). Đáp án A đúng.

questions.prompt: What would the writer say about Karina?

options.text: She’s a young girl who’s achieved a lot by becoming a national diving champion – and all with very little support.
She’s made enormous progress in a very short time – after only a couple of years, she’s already showing great signs of success.
She has a lot of natural talent, but she’s already thinking of having a break from the high board for a while.

questions.explanationVi: Đoạn 4 khẳng định: 'Fortunately, though, Karina’s coach noticed her talent and helped her develop her techniques. After only two years, she’s winning competitions in her area.' (Chỉ sau 2 năm, cô đã giành chiến thắng tại các giải đấu trong khu vực — tiến bộ vượt bậc trong thời gian ngắn). Đáp án B đúng.

tasks.title: Part 1: Short Recordings
tasks.instructions: There are 7 questions in this part. For each question, listen to the recording TWICE and choose the correct answer A, B, or C.
tasks.transcript:
1. Which T-shirt does the boy decide to buy?
Boy: I’d like to buy a black T-shirt with short sleeves, please. Large size.
Woman: I’m afraid the black ones have long sleeves, but we’ve got short sleeves in the lighter colours. Do you want a round neck or a V-neck?
Boy: It must be round neck. Let me think … umm, OK, I’ll take one of the short-sleeved ones, the colour’s not so important really.

2. Who will be on the stage next?
Man: And that was Shark, with Jo on piano and Rich on guitar. Lots of music to come, including The Three Biscuits with songs from their new CD. But first, here are Subway – you all know the drummer and guitarist, but singing here with them for the first time is Sarah Ireland, the drummer’s sister – please give her a big welcome.

3. What time will the pie be ready?
Girl: What time is it, Mum? Do you think the apple pie will be ready yet?
Mum: It’s 4.35.
Girl: And the pie went into the oven at a quarter past four?
Mum: That’s right. You could check it at five and turn the heat down a bit but don’t take it out until twenty past. That’s forty-five minutes to go!
Girl: OK, I’m hungry already.

4. Which photo does the girl dislike?
Girl: I’ve got the photos back! Look, this one of us on the beach is just brilliant!
Boy: Yes … You must get a copy for me to put in my photo album. It was a great day, but that other one’s good too!
Girl: I don’t know why you think so, that dress I’m wearing looks awful. I only bought it because it was half-price. The one of us on the boat isn’t bad, look.
Boy: Mm … apart from the fact that we look seasick!

5. What should the students take on the school trip?
Teacher: Now, you won’t need any money for the bus or your entrance ticket to the museum tomorrow, because that’s already paid for. But bring some change for when you get thirsty and want to buy a drink. The only food or drink allowed on the bus is fruit. Bring some with you because it’s quite a long trip, and you’ll get hungry. And you’ll need to bring all your coloured pencils for the work I’m going to ask you to do there.

6. Where do the boys decide to go?
Boy 1: So, we’ve got three hours. Shall we go skateboarding in the park? What do you think?
Boy 2: Well, there’s the latest space film, which is meant to be good, or there’s a new computer-game shop which has just opened.
Boy 1: Oh, well I haven’t got enough money to buy a new game anyway. Let’s go and watch the film.
Boy 2: OK. We can go skateboarding any time.

7. What has the girl lost?
Teacher: Can I help you? You look worried. Is everything all right?
Girl: Well, I was in the playground about ten minutes ago with my friends and I got a call on my mobile phone – I had to get a pen out of my bag to write something down and I think my purse fell out. I can’t find it now. Do you know if anyone has handed it in?
Teacher: You know you’re not supposed to bring phones to school – anyway, let me go and check. What colour is it?

tasks.title: Part 2: Short Conversations
tasks.instructions: There are 7 questions in this part. Listen to the conversations TWICE and choose the correct answer A, B, or C.
tasks.transcript:
8. You will hear two friends talking about a play.
Boy: Hey, what happened to you? You just disappeared from the theatre yesterday.
Girl: Erm, well, I did tell the teacher I wanted to leave.
Boy: What was wrong? I didn’t think the play was that terrible?
Girl: It was nothing to do with that. You know what it’s like when you get toothache, though – you can’t concentrate on anything. The teacher phoned my mum who contacted the dentist, but they couldn’t see me yesterday, even though it was a bit of an emergency. So I had to go this morning.
Boy: It seems you’ll do anything to avoid going to the theatre!

9. You will hear two friends talking about the food at a school party.
Girl: The party was fun, wasn’t it?
Boy: It was. It was a bit of a shame that everyone was told to bring anything they wanted, rather than making a list of who should bring what.
Girl: Yes, it certainly meant that lots of people brought the same thing.
Boy: Not having lots of stuff to choose from doesn’t bother me as long as you like what’s there, which I did.
Girl: Me too. I didn’t see anyone eating what I brought – apart from us of course.
Boy: No, but that meant there was more for us.

10. You will hear two friends talking about a soccer match they both watched on TV.
Girl: Did you see the soccer match last night?
Boy: Sure did, and although I can’t say I was unhappy at the result, it wasn’t the most interesting game I’ve ever seen.
Girl: They’ve played better, I agree, but I didn’t think they did that badly, especially that guy you really like.
Boy: He did well, but he was the only one who did. Imagine if he got injured and couldn’t play for a few weeks – they’d lose every game.
Girl: Let’s hope that never happens. Anyway, I thought it was a pretty entertaining game.
Boy: I’ve seen our school team play more interesting soccer.

11. You will hear two friends talking about a new science building at their school.
Boy: Have you been in the new science building yet?
Girl: I had a class in there this morning. It’s a shame they’ve used all the stuff for experiments from the old building.
Boy: Yes, it’d be nice to have new things like that as well as a new building. What do you think of it inside?
Girl: The colours are nice and those paintings make it look really modern.
Boy: I don’t think we share the same taste in colours and paintings, but I’m really impressed with the design of the outside.
Girl: I can’t think of a building I like the look of more.

12. You will hear a girl talking about a blog she has started writing.
Boy: Have you started your blog yet?
Girl: I’ve already written five entries and have had nice comments from some readers. That really makes it seem like it was worth doing, despite all the issues I had when I was getting it ready. The website used said it was easy to create a blog – and maybe it is for someone who’s a bit more familiar with IT than I am.
Boy: Have you put pictures in, too?
Girl: A few. I think I need more, though, to get it looking as good as some of the other blogs I’ve seen.

13 & 14. You will hear a girl telling her friend about learning Chinese.
Boy: Are you still enjoying your Chinese lessons?
Girl: I am, but we always focus on reading and writing. I know they’re important, but I want to learn other skills, too.
Boy: There’s loads of stuff online for improving reading and writing, but less for speaking, I guess. It’s the same problem with coursebooks – they’re good for exercises on grammar and things, but you obviously can’t talk to a book!
Girl: No …
Boy: But lots of people learn Chinese these days, so there must be groups that meet just to practise talking to each other. Why not search for one of those?
Girl: Hmm, maybe.

tasks.title: Part 3: Extended Conversation (True / False)
tasks.instructions: There are 6 questions in this part. You will hear Lisa and Sam talking about a book they have both read. Decide whether statements 15 to 20 are Correct (True) or Incorrect (False). Choose A for True and B for False.
tasks.transcript:
You will hear a girl called Lisa and a boy called Sam talking about a book they have both read.

Lisa: So, Sam, have you finished that book we had to read for school, Lime Country?
Sam: Oh, hi, Lisa. Yeah, just last weekend. It took me a long time to get into it. The first chapter was difficult. But in the end I couldn’t put it down.
Lisa: I liked it from the first page. I’ve never finished a book so quickly, and normally I don’t like reading fiction.
Sam: The main character in the story, Paul, was interesting. He hurt his leg badly and couldn’t play football with the other kids. But the author didn’t make you feel pity for him.
Lisa: Yes, that was because he was such a strong character. He couldn’t do anything active, but he used his time to think about game plans for his team. They depended on him in the end.
Sam: He was almost like a coach.
Lisa: I thought the book was well written and it had a good plot. There was a bit of mystery about Paul’s brother. Did he cause Paul’s injury? Was he jealous of Paul? You don’t find out until the very end.
Sam: I didn’t care so much about that. It was the football matches I liked, seen through Paul’s eyes. I could imagine exactly what was happening.
Lisa: The author was clever because when Paul was unhappy, the whole story – the weather, the background – sort of got darker, so the reader could feel what Paul was feeling.
Sam: There was quite a lot of detail about the techniques of football. I think the author got that just right.
Lisa: Any more would make it too long, and boring for people who weren’t mad about football. That side of the book was about right. For me, the best part was that Paul realised what’s important in life and how to deal with tough situations. He really grew as a person.

questions.prompt: Lisa disliked the book when she first started reading it.
questions.explanationVi: Lisa khẳng định: 'I liked it from the first page. I’ve never finished a book so quickly' (Tớ thích cuốn sách ngay từ trang đầu tiên). Người thấy chương đầu khó đọc là Sam chứ không phải Lisa. Đáp án B (False) đúng.

Lisa: I thought the book was well written and it had a good plot. There was a bit of mystery about Paul’s brother. Did he cause Paul’s injury? Was he jealous of Paul? You don’t find out until the very end.
Sam: I didn’t care so much about that. It was the football matches I liked, seen through Paul’s eyes. I could imagine exactly what was happening.
Lisa: The author was clever because when Paul was unhappy, the whole story – the weather, the background – sort of got darker, so the reader could feel what Paul was feeling.
Sam: There was quite a lot of detail about the techniques of football. I think the author got that just right.
Lisa: Any more would make it too long, and boring for people who weren’t mad about football. That side of the book was about right. For me, the best part was that Paul realised what’s important in life and how to deal with tough situations. He really grew as a person.

topicChoices.topic: Write a paragraph about how traveling helps people understand the world.
guidelines: Experiencing different cultures, traditions, and local cuisines directly
Meeting new people and learning to respect different lifestyles
Broadening knowledge beyond what is taught in books

topicChoices.topic: Write a paragraph about why doing part-time jobs is good for students.
guidelines: Gaining practical work experience and communication skills
Learning how to manage time and value hard-earned money
Becoming more independent and confident before graduation

writingPrompts.sampleAnswer: Traveling is one of the best and most enjoyable ways to help people understand the world around them. First of all, when we visit new places, we have a wonderful chance to experience different cultures, local festivals, and traditional cuisines directly rather than just watching them on television or the internet. Secondly, traveling allows us to meet local residents and listen to their daily stories, which teaches us to respect different lifestyles, customs, and points of view. Finally, seeing historical monuments and natural wonders with our own eyes broadens our knowledge far beyond textbooks and gives us unforgettable real-life lessons. In conclusion, traveling makes us more open-minded, tolerant, and knowledgeable citizens in our modern society.

cueCards.sampleResponse: A person that I deeply admire is my high school English teacher, Mrs. Lan. She has been teaching English for more than fifteen years and always prepares creative, engaging lessons for her students. I admire her not only for her wide knowledge but also for her patience and kindness. Whenever any student feels shy about speaking English, she encourages us warmly and helps us build confidence step by step.

furtherQuestions: Do you prefer traveling with family or with friends?

cueCards.sampleResponse: A memorable trip that I still remember clearly is my family vacation to Ha Long Bay last summer. During the two-day trip, we took a boat tour around the limestone islands, explored a huge cave, and ate delicious fresh seafood on board. In the afternoon, my brother and I went kayaking in the calm green water. I felt very happy and relaxed because it was a wonderful time for my family to bond together.
